newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds ended higher with thin volume playing a big part in the last few minutes of trade as markets reacted positively to U.S. durable goods orders released on Friday.
The March pit-traded 10-year bond closed up 30 points, the last third of which happened in the closing minutes as what little volume there was sent the market through key resistance.
About 12 points of the rise came earlier on news that U.S. durable goods orders unexpectedly fell 1.6 percent in November.
Economists had expected a slight rise.
Pibor futures, closing half an hour before the late flurry in the bond pit, ended the day up one point at 96.69 for March.
Traders said the importance of Friday's moves was pushed to one side by volume at around a tenth of an average trading day. The March bond contract barely scraped together 15,000 lots.
"As usual some are using an empty market to push the market up to get the best settlement price on December 31," said one trader, who doubted the market had momentum to go much further.
Next targets were seen at 129.42, then the 129.50-52 zone.
The franc was a touch firmer at 3.3731/35 per mark in late Friday trading against 3.3747/52 per mark on Thursday.
